applies_if: Your contract involves covered defense information (CUI on nonfederal systems)
You are a subcontractor receiving CUI from a prime

deadlines.label: Malicious software submission
deadlines.value: When DoD requests it after your report

clauses.plain: The core cybersecurity clause. If your contract touches CUI, this is the one that holds you to NIST 800-171 and makes you report incidents fast.
requires: Implement all 110 NIST SP 800-171 security requirements to safeguard covered defense information
Report cyber incidents to DoD within 72 hours of discovery
Preserve and protect images and access to affected systems for DoD investigation
Submit malicious software discovered to DoD when requested
Flow these requirements down to every subcontractor that will handle covered defense information
clauses.title: Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
watch_out: The 72-hour clock starts at discovery, not when you finish investigating. Report first, investigate in parallel.
You need an incident response capability before you need it. No plan means no way to meet the deadline.
Flow-down is mandatory. If your sub causes the incident, the prime answers for it.
Rapid reporting is a contract obligation, not optional cooperation.

applies_if: You are bidding on a solicitation that will involve covered defense information
clauses.plain: The pre-award promise. Before DoD gives you the contract, you represent that you will comply with the safeguarding controls.
requires: Represent that you intend to implement the NIST SP 800-171 safeguarding controls
Notify the contracting officer of any security requirement you cannot implement (via the variance process)
clauses.title: Compliance with Safeguarding Covered Defense Information Controls
watch_out: This is a representation to the government. Getting it wrong is a False Claims Act risk, not just a paperwork issue.
If you cannot implement a requirement, say so through the proper channel. Silence is not a strategy.

applies_if: Your contract includes 252.204-7012 (it travels with it)
clauses.plain: Protects your incident reports from being used against you competitively. DoD limits how it can use and share what you report.
requires: Acknowledge DoD's right to use cyber incident information you report for cybersecurity and law enforcement purposes
DoD is restricted from using your reported information for competitive or commercial advantage
clauses.title: Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Third-Party Contractor Reported Cyber Incident Information
watch_out: This clause exists to encourage reporting. Fear of your incident data leaking to competitors is addressed here, read it.
It does not shield you from liability for the underlying security failure.

applies_if: You are bidding on a DoD solicitation that requires an assessment score

deadlines.label: Assessment currency
deadlines.value: Valid for 3 years from assessment date

clauses.plain: The warning label. It tells bidders: you need a current NIST 800-171 assessment in SPRS or you cannot win this contract.
requires: Have a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD assessment (Basic, Medium, or High) posted in SPRS at time of award
Basic assessments are contractor self-assessments; Medium and High are government-led
clauses.title: Notice of NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
watch_out: No SPRS score at award time means no award. Posting takes planning, not minutes.
Your posted score is visible to contracting officers. A low score wins fewer bids.
This is the notice; 252.204-7020 is the actual requirement.

applies_if: Your contract was awarded under a solicitation containing 252.204-7019

deadlines.label: Assessment currency
deadlines.value: Valid for 3 years from assessment date

clauses.plain: The requirement behind the notice. Spells out which assessment level applies and what the government can verify.
requires: Maintain the required assessment level (Basic self-assessment at minimum, higher when the solicitation demands it)
Provide the government access to verify assessment results when required (Medium/High assessments)
Keep assessment information current in SPRS
clauses.title: NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
watch_out: A Basic assessment is your own work, but the scoring methodology is fixed. Score it the way DoD scores it.
Higher-value or higher-risk contracts can require Medium or High assessments performed by the government.

applies_if: Your solicitation or contract specifies a CMMC level
clauses.plain: The CMMC clause. When a solicitation specifies a CMMC level, you must hold a current certification at that level.
requires: Hold a current CMMC assessment at the level specified in the solicitation
Have the assessment status posted in SPRS
Flow CMMC requirements to subcontractors that handle CUI or FCI as specified
clauses.title: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Requirements
watch_out: As of September 2026: Phase 1 (self-assessments for Level 1, C3PAO assessments for Level 2) is in effect. Phase 2 was suspended July 13, 2026 pending reform review.
Level 1 covers safeguarding Federal Contract Information (FCI). Level 2 covers CUI and maps to the 110 NIST 800-171 requirements.
Do not confuse a NIST 800-171 self-assessment score with a CMMC certification. They are different credentials.

clauses.plain: The cloud disclosure. You tell the government whether you use cloud services in performing the contract.
requires: Represent whether cloud computing services will be used in performance of the contract
clauses.title: Representation of Use of Cloud Computing
watch_out: Answering yes triggers 252.239-7010 obligations. Know your cloud footprint before you bid.
SaaS tools count. If CUI touches your cloud apps, this matters.

applies_if: You use cloud services to store, process, or transmit DoD information under the contract
clauses.plain: The cloud security bar. Cloud services handling DoD information must meet federal cloud security baselines.
requires: Use cloud services that meet the FedRAMP Moderate baseline (or equivalent) when handling DoD information
Ensure the cloud service provider complies with incident reporting and access requirements
Flow down cloud security requirements as applicable
clauses.title: Cloud Computing Services
watch_out: Your cloud provider's compliance does not automatically make you compliant. Shared responsibility means your configuration is still on you.
Check your provider's FedRAMP Marketplace listing and know which baseline they hold.

quiz.q: Will you handle CUI (covered defense information) under this contract?
quiz.yes_note: 7012 is the core obligation: implement all 110 NIST 800-171 requirements and report incidents within 72 hours.

quiz.no_note: Without a current assessment in SPRS, you cannot be awarded contracts that require one. Use the SPRS Score Calculator to score yourself first.
quiz.q: Do you have a current NIST 800-171 assessment posted in SPRS?
Are you a subcontractor (rather than the prime)?
quiz.yes_note: As a sub, verify the prime flowed 7012 down to you. If CUI reaches you without the clause, both of you have a problem.

quiz.q: Will CUI touch any cloud service (SaaS, IaaS, hosted email, file sharing)?
quiz.yes_note: Disclose cloud use and confirm your providers meet the required baselines. Your configuration is still your responsibility.

quiz.q: Does the solicitation specify a CMMC level?
quiz.yes_note: You will need a current CMMC assessment at that level. Phase 1 rules apply; Phase 2 is suspended pending reform review.
